( 1) This Order may be cited as the Deposit Protection Order, 20 10 and shall on 1st. January, 2011.

(2) The long title of this Order is "An Order for the administration of a protection scheme, to establish the Brunei Darussalam Deposit Protection and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto".

In this Order, unless the context otherwise requires - "assessment year", in relation to the calculation and payment of premiums this Order, means the period beginning on the first day of January and on the 31st. day of December of each year or such other period as may be approved by the Minister; means the Authority as stated in the Banking Order, 2006 (S 45/2006), the Islamic Banking Order, 2008 (S 96/2008) and in the case of the Finance Companies Act (Chapter 89), the Minister; means the board of directors of the Corporation; means the chairman of the Board; "chief executive officer" means the chief executive of the Corporation; means the Brunei Darussalam Deposit Protection Corporation by section 3; means a deposit as defined in section 2(3) of the Banking Order, 2006 (S 45/2006), a deposit as defined in section 2(3) of the Islamic Banking (S 96/2008) and a deposit as defined in section 2 of the Finance Companies Act (Chapter 89), as the case may be; means a person{a) whose account has been or is to be credited in respect of monies constituting a deposit or part of such deposit; or · {b) to whom a member institution is liable in respect of an instrument issued for monies constituting a deposit or part of such deposit; "deposit protection" means the protection provided to the depositors of a institution in case of its failure to pay its deposits; means a director of the Board; "financial institution 11 means a bank licensed under section 4 or 23 of the Banking Order, 2006 (S 45/2006), an Islamic bank licensed under section 4 or 23 of the Islamic Banking Order, 2008 (S 96/2008) and a finance company under section 3 of the Finance Companies Act (Chapter 89); means the Laws of Islam according to the Syafeite, Hanafi, or Hanbali Sect of the Ahli Sunnah Waljamaah; institution" means any financial institution deemed to be a member under section 27 whose membership has not been cancelled under 31 or terminated under section 32; means the Minister of Finance; "protected deposits" means the deposits protected pursuant to section 45.

DARUSSALAM DEPOSIT PROTECTION CORPORATION Establishment of Corporation.

(1) hereby established the "Brunei Darussalam Deposit Protection {2) The Corporation shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal with power, subject to this Order, to acquire and dispose of property and may sue and be sued in its corporate name.

(3) All deeds, documents and other instruments requiring the seal of the Corporation shall be sealed with the common seal of the Corporation by the of the Corporation in the presence of the chief executive officer or a of the Corporation and of some other person duly authorised by the Corporation to act in that behalf, and shall be signed by the chief executive officer or member of the Corporation, as the case may be, and by that duly authorised person, and such signing shall be sufficient evidence that the common seal of the Corporation has been duly and properly affixed and that the seal is the lawful seal of the Corporation.

(4) The Corporation may by resolution or otherwise appoint an officer of the any other agent either generally or in a particular case to execute or sign on behalf of the Corporation any agreement or other instrument not under seal in relation to any matter coming within the powers of the Corporation. of Corporation.

(1) The Board shall meet as often as may be required but not less than 4 times a year.

(2) The chairman shall preside at all meetings of the Board and in his the directors present shall elect a chairman among the directors and the so elected shall preside and have all the powers of the chairman.

(3) The quorum for a meeting of the Board shall be a simple majority.

(4) The decisions of the Board shall be adopted by a simple majority of the present and voting.

(5) In the case of an equality of votes, the chairman shall have a casting vote.

(6) A resolution in writing, signed by all the directors, shall be as valid and effectual as if it had been passed at a meeting of the directors duly convened and held.

(7) in this section shall prevent the chairman from authorising a director to use live video, television links or other appropriate communication or multimedia facilities to participate in any meeting of the Board. Board may make by-laws.

(1) The Board may make such by-laws as are necessary or expedient in to the administration, management, control, business, assets and affairs of the Corporation including -

(a) the functions, powers, duties, remuneration, benefits and terms and conditions of services, code of conduct or surcharge on officers, employees and agents of the Corporation; {b) the conflicts of interest in respect of serving directors, officers and of the Corporation and those directors, officers and employees who have left the service of the Corporation; (cJ the appointment, terms of reference and activities of committees by the Corporation; (d} the rules and procedures to be observed by the directors at Board or (e} such other matters as may be required to be provided for under the by-laws in this Order.

(2) made under this section shall be binding on all persons to whom the by-laws apply. (3 Any person who does not comply with the by-laws made under {1)(b} is guilty of an offence under this Order. Appointment, functions and accountability.

{1) The chief executive officer shall be appointed by His Majesty the Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan.

(2) the Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan may, as His Majesty deems necessary appoint the chief executive officer to be a member of the Board.

(3) The chief executive officer shall be responsible for the day-to-day administration of the business and affairs of the Corporation. {4) The chief executive officer shall be answerable and accountable to the Board for the exercise of his powers and the performance of his duties.

(5) In the absence or incapacity of the chief executive officer, the Board may authorise a director of the Corporation to perform the duties, functions and responsibilities of the chief executive officer. Terms and conditions of service.

The chief executive officer shall{a} be deemed to be an officer or employee of the Corporation and be the terms and conditions of service as may be determined by the and (bJ enjoy such compensation and such other amenities as approved by the Minister, upon recommendation of the Board. Appointments, terms and conditions of service.

(2) or employee of the Corporation shall act in good faith and with such requirements, standards, duties and code of conduct as set out by the Board.

(3) The Corporation may, with the approval of the Board, establish and a pension or provident fund for its officers and employees out of the monies of the Corporation. Preservation of secrecy.

(2) Any person who contravenes subsection (1) is guilty of an offence and liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $50,000, imprisonment for a term not exceeding 3 years or both. Restriction on enquiring specifically into affairs of particular customer.

Without prejudice to the powers of inspection, examination, investigation, or resolution conferred on the Corporation, nothing in this Order shall {a) authorise the Minister to direct the Corporation; or {b) authorise the Corporation, to inquire specifically into the affairs of any customer of a member institution.

(1) For the purposes of this Order, the Corporation shall maintain and fund which shall comprise - {a} all premiums received by the Corporation under this Order; and fb} all other monies and assets which may in any manner become lawfully payable to, and received by or vested in the Corporation relating to any matter incidental to its powers, duties and functions,

(2) The Corporation is empowered - fa) to credit all direct operating income to, or charge all expenses, costs and losses against the fund; or fb) where such income, expenses, costs or losses cannot be specifically attributed to the fund, such credit or charge shall be proportional to the of premiums collected in the assessment year prior to the year in such credit or charge is made.

(3) In relation to the first assessment year of the Corporation, such credit or under subsection (2)(b) shall be determined by the Corporation. Borrowing power of Corporation.

(1) The Corporation, may borrow from the Consolidated Fund or raise funds manner and upon such terms and conditions as may be approved by the with the approval of His Majesty the Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan.

(2) Any borrowing from the Consolidated Fund or raising of funds as in subsection (1) shall be in accordance with Hukum Syara'. Permitted investments.

The financial year of the Corporation shall begin on the 1st. day of January and end on the 31st. day of December of each year except that the first financial year of the Corporation shall begin on the date of commencement of this Order and end on 31st. December of the following year.

(1) The accounts of the Corporation shall be audited annually(a) by the Auditor General; or

(b) by any person who has been authorised to perform the duties by the Companies Act (Chapter 39) to be performed by an auditor who shall be appointed annually by His Majesty the Sultan and Yang

(2) Where the accounts have been audited under subsection (l)(b), they may be verified by the Auditor General before a copy is submitted to the Minister. Financial statement and annual report.

The Corporation shall within 3 months from the close of its financial year a copy of the annual accounts and annual report on the operations of the throughout the year to the Minister, who shall subsequently submit to the Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan.

PROTECTION Membership, cancellation and termination Definition of deposit.

(1) Every financial institution is deemed to be a member institution from the of this Order.

(2) Any financial institution licensed after the commencement of this Order be deemed to be a member institution from the date it was granted a licence section 4 or 23 of the Banking Order, 2006 !S 45/2006), section 4 or 23 of the Islamic Banking Order, 2008 (S 96/2008) or section 3 of the Finance Companies 89), as the case may be. from membership.

(2) The Minister may, with the approval of His Majesty the Sultan and Yang by notification published in the Gazette, exempt a financial institution referred to in subsection (1) from the requirement under section 27(1).

(3) The Minister may require an applicant to furnish him with such or documents as the Minister considers necessary in relation to the application.

(4) Without prejudice to the generality of subsection (2), the Minister shall, in determining whether to grant an exemption under subsection (2), have regard to {a} the scope of deposit-taking business conducted by the financial institution in Brunei Darussalam; and

(b) in the case of a financial institution which is incorporated in a other than Brunei Darussalam -

(i) the deposits accepted by its branches and offices within Brunei Darussalam are protected by a deposit protection scheme, or any other scheme of a similar nature, and maintained in the jurisdiction in which the financial institution is incorporated (referred to in this section as the foreign deposit protection scheme}; and Iii) whether the scope and level of protection available to those under the foreign deposit protection scheme, or any scheme of a similar nature are not less than the scope and protection that would be available to the deposits the scheme if those deposits were protected by the \5) The Minister may, by notice in writing, impose on an exempt member such conditions or restrictions relating to the exemption as the Minister may think fit.

(6) The Minister may at any time - {a} by notice in writing to an exempt member institution, add to, vary or revoke any existing condition or restriction imposed by the Minister under

(5); or {b} by notice in writing impose such conditions or restrictions as the may think fit on a class of exempt member institution.

(7) An exempt member institution shall comply with all conditions or imposed on it under subsection (5) or (6), as the case may be.

(8) Any exempt member institution which contravenes subsection (7) is of an offence and liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $100,000 and, in the case of a continuing offence, to a further fine of $10,000 for every day or part thereof during which the offence continues after conviction. of exemption.

Deposits by amalgamating institutions etc.

(1) a person has deposits with 2 or more member institutions that amalgamate and continue in operation as one member institution (in this Chapter the "amalgamated institution"), a deposit of that person with an amalgamating institution on the day on which the amalgamated institution is formed, less any withdrawal from the deposit, shall be deemed to be and continue to be separately protected by the deposit protection scheme for a period of 2 years or upon maturity or until withdrawal, whichever is earlier, after the amalgamating institution becomes part of the amalgamated institution.

(2) made by a person referred to in subsection (1) with an amalgamated institution after the day on which the amalgamated institution is formed shall be protected by the deposit protection scheme only to the extent that the aggregate of that person's deposits with the amalgamated institution is less than $50,000.

(3) a member institution acquires the deposits of another member or amalgamating institution, those deposits, less any withdrawal from the deposits, shall continue to remain in the deposit protection scheme separately from any protected deposit up to the coverage limit of $50,000 for a period of or upon maturity or until withdrawal, whichever is earlier, after the date of acquisition. 14) A member institution shall maintain such records as necessary for the of subsections (1) and (2).
